findings.title: Linux fallback discards ordinary objdump instruction lines
findings.evidence: _disassemble_system_cli selects objdump -d at line 271, then skips every line containing a colon unless it starts with 0x (281). Ordinary objdump address lines use ADDRESS: without 0x. ELF metadata has no sections (181), so Capstone also returns empty (203-213).
findings.trigger: Analyze an ELF file on Linux using disassemble_section.
findings.impact: The advertised ELF disassembly and resulting CFG are empty even for a valid executable.

findings.title: Conditional branch classification omits common branch instructions
findings.evidence: The finite is_branch list at 229-244 excludes x86 jle/jge/ja/jae/jb/jbe and ARM b.ge/b.le/b.hi/b.ls. build_cfg only splits and links instructions marked is_branch at 342-347 and 373-385.
findings.trigger: Disassemble code containing one of the omitted conditional branches using Capstone.
findings.impact: CFG treats the branch as a normal instruction, omits its target edge and can merge multiple basic blocks, yielding incorrect control-flow analysis.

findings.title: Manuscript presents scripted simulation as empirical LLM comparison
findings.evidence: Lines 115-132 describe independent LLM configurations, observed budget acknowledgements and proof of semantic failure. benchmarks/run_ablation_matrix.py:29-32 returns a fixed 1000 tokens; 67-70 explicitly programs the soft overshoot; 52 and 113 assign violation counts by formula/constant. The gate used there is Python (src/spinal_gate.py:82-98), whereas manuscript:106 claims native code.
findings.trigger: Use the paper table and analysis as evidence for LLM budget compliance or native runtime confinement.
findings.impact: Readers receive empirical and native-enforcement claims that this cited deterministic harness cannot establish; label results as simulation and remove unmeasured behavioral claims.

findings.title: Bearer-prefix example accepts arbitrary credentials
findings.evidence: The complete Auth example at 148-150 only checks startsWith("Bearer "); no token comparison, signature verification, issuer, audience or expiry check follows before execution proceeds.
findings.trigger: Copy the Security & Rate Limiting authentication example and send Authorization: Bearer arbitrary.
findings.impact: Any caller can pass the illustrated authentication check and reach subsequent request handling.

findings.title: GitHub Actions secret example embeds secret directly in shell program
findings.evidence: The YAML run script interpolates secrets.API_KEY directly into echo "${{ secrets.API_KEY }}" before shell evaluation; unlike the token at 167, the secret value is not passed through an environment variable.
findings.trigger: Use this example with a secret containing shell expansion syntax such as a literal command substitution.
findings.impact: The runner interprets secret contents as shell code, causing unintended command execution or corruption of the value being stored.

tool_limitations: No native codebase-memory graph tools exposed; targeted text reads used.
Static audit only; no tests, builds, runtime launches, network API validation or physical-property verification performed.
External SDK examples reviewed for self-contained defects; current API signatures not verified.
